patient_overview.name: Brendan Frami
patient_overview.description: Brendan Frami is a 46-year-old married warehouse shift worker from Edison, New Jersey, coming in for a nutrition visit after his wellness exam flagged his weight and his dentist finished treating his gingivitis. He has lived with a curved spine since his teens and has been missing several teeth since his thirties, and he comes across as nervous and quick to apologize, as if he's bracing to be scolded about his eating. He knows his weight and diet need work but feels torn and overwhelmed about where to start, especially with a packed house of seven and a tight budget. He tends to shrug and say 'whatever you think is best' rather than push back, even when something won't actually work for his schedule or wallet.

demographics.occupation: Forklift operator and shift supervisor at a regional distribution warehouse, part-time/temporary hours
demographics.cultural_context: Brendan grew up in a working-class New Jersey family where big portions at dinner were a sign of love and nobody talked much about nutrition. He married young, and food in his house has always been about getting everyone fed fast and cheap rather than about any particular tradition. He doesn't see himself as having a 'diet' at all, just a schedule that doesn't leave room for sit-down meals.

medical_history: Concussion injury of brain (2023-05 to 2023-08, resolved)
Concussion with no loss of consciousness (2023-05 to 2023-08, resolved)
Removal of subgingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2026-09-06)
Removal of supragingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2026-09-06)
current_symptoms: Low back and shoulder-blade ache after standing a long shift, which he links to his crooked spine
Gets short of breath walking up the stairs at the warehouse
Avoids chewing on the left side where he's missing teeth
Afternoon energy crashes that he fixes with a vending-machine soda and chips
Occasional heartburn after late, greasy drive-through dinners
clinical_findings: Visibly carries extra weight through the abdomen, consistent with recorded BMI of 31
Mild asymmetry of the shoulders and rib cage on observation, consistent with his longstanding adolescent scoliosis
Several missing posterior teeth visible when he speaks or smiles, with healthy-looking gums post-treatment
Appears tired and a little fidgety, picking at his sleeve while answering questions

supplements_and_otc: Tums for heartburn, keeps a roll in his truck
Men's one-a-day multivitamin his daughter bought him, takes it 'when I remember'
Ibuprofen for back pain a few times a week

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Irregular, grazing pattern built around shift schedule: vending machine snacks and gas-station coffee during work, fast food on the way home, bigger meal late at night with family
food_preferences: Bacon egg and cheese on a hard roll
Honey buns and peanut butter crackers from the vending machine
Diet soda during the day, regular soda at night
Meatball subs and pizza on weekends
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: How often he skips lunch entirely and 'makes up for it' at 9pm
Whether he's choosing softer foods because chewing is uncomfortable with missing teeth
How much of his food budget goes to drive-through versus groceries
Late-night eating with the kids while watching TV
Use of soda and energy drinks to get through the second half of his shift
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: No consistent breakfast; grabs something from vending machine or gas station around 10am; often no real lunch; large dinner around 9-9:30pm after his shift ends, sometimes a second smaller meal if he's hungry before bed
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly soda and coffee through the day; says he 'forgets' to drink water at work because the only tap is far from his station
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: On his feet most of his shift lifting and moving pallets, but little intentional exercise outside work; back pain from his scoliosis limits weekend activity
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Quit smoking four years ago when his first grandchild was born; drinks a few beers on weekends, audit-c score suggests light-to-moderate drinking
nutrition_profile.sleep: Irregular, 5-6 hours most nights because of rotating shift start times, naps on days off

psychosocial_profile.personality: Anxious, apologetic, braces himself for criticism before anyone says anything negative
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Soft-spoken, says 'whatever you think is best' instead of stating a preference, apologizes for taking up the clinician's time, needs direct reassurance that he's not in trouble
goals: Have enough energy to play with his grandchild without getting winded
Stop his back from aching by the end of a shift
Get his weight down before his next physical
concerns: Being lectured again by his kids about his eating
That his missing teeth make him look older and unhealthy
Whether his insurance will cover more dental work if he loses more teeth
beliefs: Thinks because he's always been a 'big guy' there's not much he can do about his weight now
Believes vending machine food is just 'what you eat' when you work shifts, not really a choice
Worries healthy food costs too much for a family of seven
motivations: Wanting to be around and active for his grandchild
Pressure from his adult children who mean well but lecture him
Not wanting another scolding at his next check-up
fears: Ending up unable to work because of his back
Losing more teeth and not being able to afford to fix it
Disappointing his kids by not changing
barriers: Rotating shift schedule with no real break for meals
Tight household budget feeding seven people
Chewing discomfort from missing teeth limiting food choices
Chronic back pain from scoliosis limiting activity and standing to cook
strengths: Shows up to appointments and follows through on dental care
Genuinely wants to be healthier for his grandchild
Open and honest once he feels safe
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Married, lives with wife and large household including adult children who check in on him but tend to lecture rather than help practically
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Contemplation: aware his eating and weight are problems, feels torn between wanting change and not knowing how to fit it into his schedule or budget

initial_information: Mentions he just finished some dental work for gum disease
Says his back has ached since he was a teenager because of his scoliosis
Admits his weight has crept up over the years
Says he works odd shifts and eats 'whenever he can'
discoverable_information: Describes his typical vending-machine and drive-through eating pattern
Mentions his adult children frequently comment on his weight
Reveals he quit smoking four years ago when his grandchild was born
Explains that chewing is harder since he lost some teeth
Shares that he drinks a few beers most weekends
reluctant_information: Admits, if asked gently, that money is tight with seven people in the house and groceries are a stretch some weeks
Reveals he sometimes skips buying his ibuprofen refill or picks the cheaper store-brand to save a few dollars
Confides that he's embarrassed his teeth look bad and avoids smiling in photos
hidden_information: Brendan has gone without paying a utility bill some months specifically to afford groceries for the household of seven
He has put off replacing worn-out work boots for over a year because the money went to food instead
He has considered picking up a second part-time job but is afraid the extra hours will make his eating and back pain worse

opportunities.learning_objective: Elicit a realistic 24-hour recall from a shift worker and identify timing-related nutrition problems.
expected_discoveries: Long gaps without food followed by a large late dinner
Heavy reliance on vending machines and drive-throughs during work hours
possible_patient_reactions: 'Honestly I don't really eat breakfast, I just grab whatever's in the machine.'
'I know it's bad, I'm sorry, I just don't have time.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Explore the connection between tooth loss and food choices without judgment.
expected_discoveries: He favors softer, easier-to-chew foods since losing teeth
He avoids certain vegetables and tougher meats
He feels self-conscious about his smile
possible_patient_reactions: 'Yeah, I kind of just avoid the crunchy stuff now.'
'I didn't think that was connected to my teeth, honestly.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Use motivational interviewing to meet him in the contemplation stage rather than pushing action.
expected_discoveries: His ambivalence about change despite knowing it matters
His fear of being lectured, which makes him shut down
His genuine motivation around his grandchild
possible_patient_reactions: 'My kids already tell me this stuff, I don't need another lecture.' said quietly

opportunities.learning_objective: Gently uncover financial barriers affecting food and health purchases.
expected_discoveries: Tight household budget for seven people
Trade-offs between groceries and other bills
Reduced adherence to OTC pain relief due to cost
possible_patient_reactions: Initially says money's fine, deflecting with 'we manage'
Later admits, 'Some months I gotta choose between the electric bill and the grocery run.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Address musculoskeletal pain (scoliosis-related back pain) as a barrier to activity and meal preparation.
expected_discoveries: Back pain limits standing to cook or grocery shop
Pain contributes to reliance on convenience food
Interest in simple, low-effort meal strategies
possible_patient_reactions: 'By the time I get home my back's killing me, cooking's the last thing I want to do.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Identify practical, low-cost, shift-friendly nutrition strategies the family can use.
expected_discoveries: Openness to simple swaps like packing food instead of vending machine snacks
Willingness to involve his wife in meal prep planning
Budget constraints that rule out some suggestions
possible_patient_reactions: 'That might work if it's not too much extra cost.'
'I'll try, but no promises, things get crazy at work.'
